memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "This is so the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they are now making in the open fields. They must bring them to the priest, that is, to the LORD, at the entrance to the tent of meeting and sacrifice them as fellowship offerings." - Lev 17:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sacrifices they are now making in the open fields. Present tense. This was not a hypothetical danger — it was already happening.

God is not addressing a theoretical problem. He knows exactly what His people are doing out in the fields, away from the tabernacle, out of sight of the priests. And He names it plainly.

There is comfort and challenge together in that. The challenge: God sees what we do when no one is watching. Nothing in all creation is hidden from God's sight (Heb 4:13). The private compromise, the habit conducted in the open field of our lives where no one from church will ever see.

The comfort: God addresses it rather than abandoning us to it. He does not walk away from a people already going wrong. He speaks, corrects, and gives them a better way.

And look at what He calls them to instead — fellowship offerings. These were the sacrifices where the worshipper shared in the meal, eating in God's presence with family and friends. God is not simply banning something. He is offering something better: come and eat with Me.

He always calls us away from something towards something.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you doing "in the open fields" away from accountability?
2. Does God's knowledge of it frighten you or comfort you?
3. What better thing might God be calling you towards?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see what I do when no one is watching. Thank You that You correct rather than abandon me. Draw me away from what harms me and into fellowship with You. Amen.
